2abc6b757313f2b4c868fa2c960b7a06d7cab880.summary: KSI Digital analysed 'Ancient', a Linux IoT botnet with a custom ANCT C2 protocol, captured in a Telnet/SSH honeypot in October 2026. Devices are infected via Telnet logins and fetch a shell dropper in three versions that adds cron and init persistence. The C2 lookup is hidden inside DNS-over-TLS, and the bot stays idle while traced. A 10-minute controlled contact confirmed the C2 live. The report also covers a Mirai kit delivered from the same loader routine, and publishes indicators and detection rules.

2a4321fdcddd7640c9c4c60ed54d73d030eaefe5.summary: Describes North Korean-aligned actors targeting macOS and their RustBucket and KandyKorn campaigns. The report finds RustBucket SwiftLoader droppers now delivering KandyKorn RAT payloads. The KandyKorn chain starts with social engineering over Discord, using a fake cryptocurrency arbitrage bot, and ends with a backdoor RAT loaded in memory. It also links ObjCShellz to SwiftLoader and reports shared infrastructure. Indicators (hashes, IP addresses, file paths) are listed by the vendor.

2a04fb97ff89595bc49dd71a7246402e3b355cc6.summary: Yoroi Z-LAB reports on ATMitch, an ATM malware sample spotted in early April and possibly active since 2017. A loader injects a DLL into the Wincor Nixdorf fwmain32.exe process using thread hijacking. The DLL uses the XFS banking interface to read commands from a file and dispense cash. The report says it is manually installed on ATMs after a network intrusion, possibly used by the Carbanak or GCMAN groups, and may be the tip of a larger attack.

2a02f9e9e4b065166a08c111990f10f362621939.summary: Mandiant's M-Trends 2023 special report. It gives 2022 investigation metrics (global median dwell time 16 days, 63% of incidents notified externally, exploits the top initial vector at 32%). Its main section covers Russian cyber operations in Ukraine from before the February 2022 invasion through December 2022, naming APT28, UNC2589, GRU edge-device compromise, wipers and hacktivist personas. It also covers North Korean financially motivated crypto operations, the credential-focused intrusions of UNC3661 and UNC3944, and a red team case study. Attributions are the report's own or are cited…

subject.name: The Invasion of Ukraine: Cyber Operations During Wartime

hedges: Mandiant suspects UNC2589 operates on behalf of Russian government interests.
Mandiant has not yet uncovered direct evidence linking KillNet to Russian Intelligence.
Mandiant does not have sufficient insight to confirm that cyber operations supported the kinetic campaign against Ukrainian energy infrastructure.
It is unclear whether the ESET-reported operation against a Ukrainian electric utility was effective in its impact on electric transmission and distribution.
Mandiant identified only suspected Turla activity, and the late 2021 compromise is described as aligning with Turla tactics.
Media reports and the UN are cited for North Korean revenue and missile funding; the regime's cryptocurrency holdings are described as allegedly held.
Mandiant assesses that the Andariel-related ransomware activity is linked based on sensitive and open source reporting that suggests it.
The increase in external notifications in 2022 is likely impacted by Mandiant's investigative support in Ukraine, which the report calls an outlier.
